notes: Fictional relation, real instances (whole numbers): a role chain through real knowledge (README, Role chains through real knowledge). Each derived query states only the made-up link; the real hop (6 divides 12, 3 divides 9) is left to the model, listed as a bridge with bridge_in_prompt false, and checked before editing. Direct no (asked as 'could it fail?'); d1 no, phrased so it discriminates: before the insert nothing ties 5 to 12, so 5 could fail to be cairn-linked to 12 (yes), after it 5 must be (no); d2 yes. Cross-lingual queries ask d1, also leaving the hop out. Near query: a real role chain in group theory (characteristic subgroup then normal subgroup gives normal subgroup). Replaces the functional 'has Tolland root' insert, whose cross-lingual and first derived 'no' held either way (discriminates: false). RBox: the made-up link is in the prompt and the real hop is a firm stored fact, so each query is determinate (no determinacy, no worlds). Locality references are the logical answers; the scoring gold is the model's own pre-edit answer.
